questions.context: En el salón de clase de un colegio de Cali hay un calendario con los días de la semana en inglés.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Sunday comes before Monday, not after it.
Correct. The order is Monday, Tuesday, so Tuesday comes after Monday.
Incorrect. Thursday comes three days after Monday, not right after it.
Incorrect. Wednesday comes after Tuesday, so it is two days after Monday.

questions.explanation: El orden de la semana es "Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday". Después del lunes ("Monday") viene el martes, "Tuesday". El domingo ("Sunday") va antes del lunes.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which two days are the weekend?
questions.context: Los sábados y domingos muchas familias de Bogotá van a la ciclovía porque no hay colegio.

options.feedback: Correct. The weekend is Saturday and Sunday, the days with no school.
Incorrect. Monday and Tuesday are school days at the start of the week.
Incorrect. Friday and Monday are school days; the weekend is between them.
Incorrect. Wednesday and Thursday are in the middle of the week.

questions.explanation: El fin de semana se dice "weekend" y son dos días: "Saturday" (sábado) y "Sunday" (domingo). De lunes a viernes son los días de colegio, llamados "weekdays" o "school days".
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: "Today is Thursday. Tomorrow is ___."
questions.context: Hoy es jueves en un colegio de Cartagena y los niños esperan la clase de educación física de mañana.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Wednesday comes before Thursday, so it was yesterday.
Incorrect. Saturday comes two days after Thursday, not tomorrow.
Incorrect. Tuesday comes before Wednesday and Thursday, so it is in the past.
Correct. Friday comes right after Thursday, so tomorrow is Friday.

questions.explanation: "Tomorrow" significa mañana, el día siguiente. Si hoy ("today") es jueves, "Thursday", el día siguiente es viernes, "Friday". "Wednesday" fue ayer ("yesterday").
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: How many days are there in one week?
questions.context: En la clase de inglés en Neiva, los niños cuentan los días de una semana en el calendario.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Five is the number of school days, Monday to Friday, not the whole week.
Incorrect. Six days is one day short; Monday to Sunday makes seven.
Incorrect. Ten is too many; a week has only seven days.
Correct. A week has seven days, from Monday to Sunday.

questions.explanation: Una semana ("week") tiene siete días: "seven days". Cinco ("five") son solo los días de colegio de lunes a viernes; si sumamos el sábado y el domingo tenemos siete.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Read: "Camila goes to school from Monday to Friday. On Saturday she visits her grandma in Bogota. On Sunday she goes to the park." When does Camila visit her grandma?
questions.context: Camila vive en Soacha y los fines de semana visita a su familia en Bogotá.

options.feedback: Incorrect. On Sunday Camila goes to the park, not to her grandma's house.
Correct. The text says "On Saturday she visits her grandma".
Incorrect. On Monday Camila goes to school, according to the text.
Incorrect. Friday is a school day for Camila, so she does not visit her grandma then.

questions.explanation: Hay que buscar en el texto la palabra "grandma" (abuela): "On Saturday she visits her grandma". El domingo va al parque y de lunes a viernes va al colegio. Con los días usamos "on": "on Saturday".
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which list is in the correct order?
questions.context: Un niño de Santa Marta ordena las tarjetas de los días para el mural del salón.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Thursday comes before Friday, so this order is wrong.
Incorrect. Wednesday comes before Thursday, so the last two are swapped.
Correct. Wednesday, Thursday and Friday follow the order of the week.
Incorrect. Saturday comes before Sunday, so the first two are swapped.

questions.explanation: Para revisar el orden hay que recordar la secuencia completa: "Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday". Solo "Wednesday, Thursday, Friday" respeta esa secuencia.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Pedro says: "Yesterday was Saturday, so today is a school day." Is Pedro right?
questions.context: Pedro se despierta en su casa de Valledupar y piensa que tiene que ir al colegio.

options.text: Yes. Today is Monday, a school day.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Monday comes after Sunday, so it is two days after Saturday.

options.text: Yes. Today is Friday, a school day.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Friday comes before Saturday, so it cannot be today.

options.text: No. Today is Sunday, and there is no school.
options.feedback: Correct. The day after Saturday is Sunday, which is part of the weekend.
Incorrect. Saturday was yesterday; the day changes, so today is Sunday.

questions.explanation: Si ayer ("yesterday") fue sábado, hoy es domingo ("Sunday"). El domingo es parte del fin de semana y no hay colegio. Por eso Pedro está equivocado: el lunes llega mañana, no hoy.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement:
Read the dialogue.
Ana: "What day is it today?"
Luis: "___"
questions.context: Ana y Luis conversan en la ruta escolar en Villavicencio.

options.feedback: Correct. The question asks for the day, and Wednesday is a day of the week.
Incorrect. "Ten o'clock" tells the time, not the day of the week.
Incorrect. July is a month of the year, not a day of the week.
Incorrect. "Sunny" describes the weather, not the day.

questions.explanation: La pregunta "What day is it today?" pide un día de la semana, por ejemplo "It's Wednesday". "Ten o'clock" es una hora, "July" es un mes y "sunny" habla del clima.
questions.subject: ingles
